posts.title: How to read your own numbers before a strategy review
posts.excerpt: Three figures to check before you call a consultant.
posts.content:
Before any strategy review, we ask owners to look at three figures: margin by product, cash over twelve months and orders by customer. Most can be found in the accounts you already have.

Write down what surprises you. Those surprises are usually the best place to start, and they make our first call far more useful for you.

posts.title: Why the middle layer decides whether a plan works
posts.excerpt: Plans are carried out by managers, not by slides.
posts.content:
A plan only works if the people between the owner and the shop floor understand it and believe in it. When it stalls, the cause is rarely the plan. It is usually unclear roles in the middle.

Start small. Name who decides what, hold one short weekly meeting and give managers the numbers they need. These steps cost little and change a great deal.

posts.title: A family-business handover takes five years, not one
posts.excerpt: Why early planning protects both the business and the family.
posts.content:
Handing over a company is not a single event. The successor needs time to learn, staff need time to trust, and the owner needs time to let go. In our experience, five years is a realistic span.

Begin with an honest conversation about timing and roles. Then write the plan down, review it each year and keep the owner involved until the handover is complete.
